# Didache Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_011_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 11

**1** Therefore, whoever comes and teaches you all these things said above, receive him.

**2** But if the teacher himself is turned away and teaches another teaching to the destruction of the above, do not listen to him; but if his teaching is to the increase of righteousness and the knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.

**3** Now concerning apostles and prophets, act according to the decree of the gospel.

**4** Let every apostle who comes to you be received as the Lord.

**5** But he shall not remain more than one day; but if there is need, even the next day; if he stays three days, he is a false prophet.

**6** But when the apostle departs, let him take nothing except bread until he reaches his next lodging place; but if he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

**7** And do not test or judge any prophet who speaks in the Spirit — for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven.

**8** But not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he has the behavior of the Lord. From the behavior, then, the false prophet and the prophet shall be known.

**9** And any prophet who orders a table in the Spirit shall not eat from it; but if he does eat from it, he is a false prophet.

**10** And every prophet who teaches the truth — if he does not do what he teaches, he is a false prophet.

**11** But every proven prophet who acts for the earthly mystery of the church, but does not teach others to do what he himself does, shall not be judged by you — for with God he has his judgment, for the ancient prophets also did in this way.

**12** But whoever says in the Spirit, "Give me money," or anything else, do not listen to him; but if he says to give to others who are in need, let no one judge him.

---

*EMET notes: V.7 — "this sin will not be forgiven" = testing a genuine prophet is equivalent to blaspheming the Holy Spirit (cf. Matt 12:31-32). V.9 — "orders a table in the Spirit" = commands that a meal be prepared while under inspiration. This may refer to an agape meal or a special prophetic feast. V.11 — "earthly mystery of the church" (μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας) is one of the most obscure phrases in the Didache. It may refer to symbolic actions (like Hosea's marriage) that enact prophetic truths — the prophet lives out what he prophesies.*
